### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/driver-sql`, `@objectstack/service-datasource`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **154** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **11** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-datasource/src/driver-catalog.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-defaults/data.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**18** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3a0aa915ae0e3838e93beace25bf14d116f3f596`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **11** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-datasource/src/driver-catalog.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-defaults/data.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **14** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **64** of **227** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **173** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3a0aa915ae0e3838e93beace25bf14d116f3f596` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `abf44de2e91aa2410ecb55a0bd35ffe90d83d2a6` — the merge of head `878bda8776341b9d9f06bfca85854c2360cdf13d` into base `3a0aa915ae0e3838e93beace25bf14d116f3f596`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin abf44de2e91aa2410ecb55a0bd35ffe90d83d2a6 && git checkout abf44de2e91aa2410ecb55a0bd35ffe90d83d2a6
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 3a0aa915ae0e3838e93beace25bf14d116f3f596 878bda8776341b9d9f06bfca85854c2360cdf13d && git checkout -B drift-repro 3a0aa915ae0e3838e93beace25bf14d116f3f596 && git merge --no-ff 878bda8776341b9d9f06bfca85854c2360cdf13d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3a0aa915ae0e3838e93beace25bf14d116f3f596
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 3a0aa915ae0e3838e93beace25bf14d116f3f596` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set and public-surface changes the diff implies, each judged against the tree:

1. **New driver id `mssql`, aliases `sqlserver` and `tedious`** — `DRIVER_VOCABULARY` gains a row `{ id: 'mssql', aliases: [], contractOnlyAliases: ['mssql', 'sqlserver', 'tedious'], hasLocalDefault: false, federationOnly: true }`, appended after `turso`. `resolveDriverId('mssql' | 'sqlserver' | 'tedious' | ' SQLServer ')` → `'mssql'`; `resolveDatabaseDriverId` → `undefined` for all three; `DATABASE_DRIVER_SELECTION_ALIASES` / `DATABASE_DRIVER_SELECTION_IDS` unchanged in content; `BUILTIN_DRIVER_IDS` gains `mssql` last. The CLI parity test pins that `os start` refuses every spelling in dev and prod even with a URL (`UnsupportedDriverError`). `DriverType` is `z.string()` with retired-spelling refusals only, so the datasource `driver` slot needs no change and accepts the three spellings. **Right** — the memory row's "contract face yes, selection face no" shape reused for a second reason, and the registry's docblock says so. One caveat on how the selection withdrawal is held, in ④ (should-fix 2).
2. **`DriverVocabularyEntry.federationOnly?: true` and its projections** — `FEDERATION_ONLY_DRIVER_IDS` (`['mssql']`, frozen, derived from the rows), `driverIsFederationOnly(driver)` (follows every alias face via `resolveDriverId`; `false` for plugin ids and non-strings — pinned), `FederationOnlyDriverId` (`Extract` over the literal rows → `'mssql'`, pinned with `expectTypeOf`), `DatabaseDriverSelectionId` (`Exclude` of it from `BuiltinDriverId`). `resolveDatabaseDriverId` and `DATABASE_DRIVER_SELECTION_IDS` narrow their TYPE from `BuiltinDriverId` to `DatabaseDriverSelectionId`; runtime values are unchanged, and the narrowing is named in the changeset body. **Right.**
3. **Federation-only refusal on a managed datasource** — `DatasourceSchema`'s superRefine: `ds.schemaMode === 'managed' && driverIsFederationOnly(ds.driver)` → one issue at path `schemaMode`. `schemaMode` defaults to `'managed'` before the refine runs, so a datasource naming the driver and nothing else is refused (pinned for `mssql` and `tedious`); `'external'` and `'validate-only'` parse (pinned). The message names the scope, the one-line fix and the drivers that can own tables, the last derived from `DATABASE_DRIVER_SELECTION_IDS` (pinned to contain every selection id and not `mssql`). The driver-side gate, `ClassHeadFacet.assertDialectEmits`, refuses every DDL operation on `MSSQL_FEDERATION_CLIENTS` with `UnsupportedDialectEmissionError(..., 'federation-only')` (code `SQL_DIALECT_EMISSION_UNSUPPORTED`) before the Postgres-wire check — pinned offline. The factory arm connects only and forwards no `autoMigrate`. Rule and gate agree. **Right.**
4. **`MssqlConfigSchema`** — closed `strictObject`: `host` (placeholder-free, required), `port` (int, default 1433), `instanceName` (optional), `database` (required), `username` (optional), `password` (a `refusedInlineCredentialKey`), `ssl` (`DriverSslToggleSchema`). Refused with guidance: `url` / `connectionString` / `dsn` / `uri` (tedious reads no connection-string grammar — true, and the factory builds an object), `autoMigrate` (no DDL emitted — consistent with #3), `pool` / `schemaMode` / `readOnly` (belong on the datasource), `ca` / `cert` / `key` / `rejectUnauthorized` / `trustServerCertificate` (belong in the datasource `ssl` block), `options` (not a passthrough — true: `buildMssqlConnection` reads the listed keys only), `passwd` / `pwd`. Aliases rename with a hint (`server` → `host` pinned). Every accepted key is read by `buildMssqlConnection` (`host` → `server`, `username` → `user`, bound secret → `password`, `instanceName` → `options.instanceName`, resolved ssl → `options.encrypt` / `trustServerCertificate` / `cryptoCredentialsDetails`). The JSON-Schema projection, the authorable-surface rows (`password [RETIRED]`) and the `dropped-refinements.baseline.json` row (`database`, `host`, `instanceName`, `username` — the four `placeholderFree` sites) follow the postgres pattern. **Right as a contract**; the TLS prose it carries is the must-fix (④.1).
5. **New exports** — `MssqlConfigSchema`, `MssqlConfig`, `MssqlConfigParsed`, `getMssqlConfigJsonSchema`, `FEDERATION_ONLY_DRIVER_IDS`, `driverIsFederationOnly`, `FederationOnlyDriverId`, `DatabaseDriverSelectionId` = the eight additions in `api-surface/data.json`; `driver/index.ts` re-exports `mssql.zod`, which `DRIVER_CONFIG_SCHEMAS` (a `Record` keyed on every `BuiltinDriverId`) makes mandatory. **Right.** Note for ③: the sibling PR publishes the same two concepts under different names.
6. **`SqlDialect` gains `'mssql'`; `DIALECT_ALIASES.mssql`** — `nvarchar` / `nchar` / `ntext` / `varchar` / `char` / `text` / `xml` / `sysname` → text; `bit` → boolean; `tinyint` / `smallint` / `int` → integer; `bigint` → bigint; `decimal` / `numeric` / `money` / `smallmoney` → decimal; `float` / `real` → float; `date` → date; `time` → time; `datetime` / `datetime2` / `smalldatetime` / `datetimeoffset` → datetime; `uniqueidentifier` → uuid; `varbinary` / `binary` / `image` / `timestamp` / `rowversion` → binary. Every type the card lists is present and pinned; `nvarchar(max)` / `varbinary(max)` / `datetime2(7)` reach their base through the existing paren strip (pinned); `timestamp` → binary overrides the shared base's datetime for this dialect only (pinned, with the postgres control); `sql_variant` / `hierarchyid` / `geography` / `geometry` → unknown so a draft flags them (pinned). The producer, `mssqlColumns`, lower-cases `INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS.DATA_TYPE`, which is exactly the spelling the table is keyed on; the first consumer, `external-datasource-service.ts`, passes the driver's `dialectName` (`'mssql'` from `ManagedDriftFacet.dialectName`) straight through `typeVocabulary`. **Right**, with one accept-set gap in ④ (should-fix 3).
7. **`SqlDialectName` gains `'mssql'`; `dialectName` answers it** — so the predicate emitters, the aggregation operand policy, `formatOutput` and the introspection arms each take an mssql arm and nothing on this client falls to `'unknown'`. The text-match arms are the #6518 contract on a case-insensitive collation: `CAST(x AS nvarchar(max)) COLLATE Latin1_General_100_BIN2` on both operands, `TRANSLATE` over the 26 letters for the fold (never `LOWER()`), `\` `%` `_` `[` escaped behind the bound `ESCAPE` (`[` because it opens a character class on SQL Server — the #5567 bypass in a fourth spelling, closed), `$like` patterns carried through `mssqlLikePattern` so a bare `[` stays literal. All pinned offline via `toSQL()`. **Right.**
8. **Metadata-protocol `added`** — a new accepted driver id, a new `config` contract (six authorable keys, `password` retired) and a new `SqlDialect` member widen what a metadata document may say; nothing is narrowed or re-read. **Right.**
9. **Driver refusals that are not spec accept-set changes** — `$contains` / `$notContains` / `$empty` on a multi-value field over mssql are `INVALID_FILTER` (withheld subtree), managed DDL is `SQL_DIALECT_EMISSION_UNSUPPORTED`, `limit: 0` compiles to `TOP (0)`, `OFFSET` without a key orders by the catalog's single-column PK or `(SELECT NULL)`, writes go through `OUTPUT inserted.*` with `includeTriggerModifications` (a temp table, so a table with an enabled trigger accepts it), `uniqueidentifier` reads back lower-case via tedious `lowerCaseGuids` unless the host set it. Read as the cited code behind the card's constraints and found consistent with the docs; pinned offline, and live on SQL Server 2022 by the dev's account (no CI job hosts it — the reporter prints `NOT RUN`, a declared skip, never a claimed pass). Not re-judged beyond that.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/31327-mssql-federation-dialect.md`: `@objectstack/spec: minor`, `@objectstack/driver-sql: minor`, `@objectstack/service-datasource: minor`. The spec diff adds a driver id, a config contract, eight exports and one `SqlDialect` member; removes nothing; changes no existing answer (`canonicalizeSqlType(x)` with no dialect or any other dialect is byte-identical; the vocabulary rows before `mssql` are untouched; `resolveDatabaseDriverId` returns the same values). The TypeScript narrowing of `resolveDatabaseDriverId()` and `DATABASE_DRIVER_SELECTION_IDS` to `DatabaseDriverSelectionId` is named in the changeset body (two in-repo consumers needed `as readonly string[]` casts, which is the cost the sentence prices). Minor is the right level for all three packages.

Clause-②: `yes (widening)` — declared identically, line-initial, on the PR body and in the changeset; the card expected it; the claim's provisional `yes` is confirmed from the diff.
Metadata-protocol: `added` — PR body and changeset agree.
Skills-docs: `generated only` on both — true of the tree (`_index.md` row only).

### ③ Boundary flags

From the os-dev-report (comment 6717835015):

- `open_questions: []` — nothing to answer.
- Out-of-scope finding 1 ("a substring operator on a uniqueidentifier column matches SQL Server's upper-case text form of the GUID; documented, equality and `$in` are exact" — carrier "PR #31381 · noted, not filed"): a PR is not a carrier, and the wrinkle is a contract wrinkle — the read path answers the GUID lower-case, the case-exact substring path compares it upper-case, so a value copied from a read into `$contains` finds nothing. **Escalated to the epic PM**: file the card (or fix it here — should-fix 4).
- "Outside the claimed surface, each forced by a gate and covered by claim amendment 2 or listed here": `scripts/check-driver-conformance.mjs` and the dropped-refinements ledger are covered by claim amendment 3; the CLI parity test, the credential-slot pin and the analytics echo-bucket roster are tests of the named packages' contracts; `scripts/check-tenant-chokepoint.mjs` (one watch-hint row for the new introspection module), the strictness-ledger row, `llms.txt` and the generated reference docs are gate-forced generated or ledger rows. Each is named in the report. Surface acceptance is the lane seat's, not this record's; nothing here changes an accept-set beyond what ① lists.
- `gates`: "Sweep on dfc8a224c5 running; its `--ran` verdict goes in a separate comment on the PR" — no such comment exists on the card; and the head's own CI lanes were cancelled (see the gate paragraph above). The gate verdicts for this head are unanswered. **Escalated**: the record that lifts the Tier H barrier must be on a head whose lanes concluded.
- `dogfood_battery: n/a` — no `!` in the title and no `(narrowing)` arm. Right.
- `tests`: live SQL Server 2022 run is the dev's account; the tree makes it an opt-in cell (`OS_TEST_MSSQL_URL`, `OS_EXPECT_MSSQL_FEDERATION=1`), reported on its own line, never a claimed pass. Right shape.

From the PR body's acceptance notes:

- IDENTITY-keyed tables cannot be written: documented in the SQL Server section ("keep a table keyed that way read-only"). Answered.
- `$contains` / `$empty` on multi-value fields refused: the driver side is right (refusing beats a substring guess); the SPEC side has a gap the body does not name — should-fix 3.
- Date buckets in memory; cross-field `$field` refused on federated objects; no single-column PK pages without a stable order and warns once: driver behaviour, documented, no spec claim depends on them. Answered.
- service-analytics' native-SQL face still emits plain `LIKE` for mssql: the card's "nothing falls through to `'unknown'`" is met in driver-sql, but the #6518 contract is now kept on one face and not the other for the same datasource. **Escalated to the epic PM** as a follow-up card (the analytics compilers' dialect vocabulary is shared, per the `mssqlAggregandOperandSql` docblock, so it is a deliberate seam, not an oversight).
- SQL Server 2017 floor (`TRANSLATE`): stated in the dialect module and the docs; the ADR amendment is dialect-list only. Answered.
- Studio connection form does not offer `mssql`: #31389 filed; the Tables tab, `list_remote_tables` and `import_object` read the introspection seam this PR provides, which is what the card's Task names. Answered.
- Eight new spec exports: matches `api-surface/data.json`. Answered.

Card constraints:

- Live cell env: card said `MSSQL_URL`; claim amendment 2 set `OS_TEST_MSSQL_URL`; the tree uses `OS_TEST_MSSQL_URL`. Answered.
- Serial with #31328 (Oracle, PR #31351): the two trees publish the SAME concept under DIFFERENT names — this tree `driverIsFederationOnly` / `DatabaseDriverSelectionId` / `managedOnFederationOnlyDriverRefusal`, the Oracle tree `isFederationOnlyDriver` / `DatabaseSelectionDriverId` / `federationOnlyDriverOnManagedRefusal`. Two of each are public spec exports. **Escalated to the epic PM**: whichever PR lands second adopts the first's names, so the spec never publishes two names for one projection in one minor (this tree's `driverIsFederationOnly` follows the registry's own `driverHasLocalDefault`; the choice is the PM's, the single-name invariant is not). For the reconciler, the single-driver hard-codes in this tree: `config-registry.test.ts` (`withheld` equals `['memory', 'mssql']`, `FEDERATION_ONLY_DRIVER_IDS` equals `['mssql']`, the `BUILTIN_DRIVER_IDS` tuple, the `expectTypeOf` pin that equates `FederationOnlyDriverId` with `'mssql'`), `driver-vocabulary-parity.test.ts` (`['mssql', 'sqlserver', 'tedious']`), the `federationOnly` docblock ("SQL Server today"), `FEDERATION_CELL_SYMBOLS`, and in driver-sql `renderFederationOnlyEmissionRefusal`, which hard-codes "(Microsoft SQL Server)" into the message and would mislabel a second federation-only client unless parameterised. The design otherwise generalises by addition: the column, the two projections, the derived refusal list, the `isFederationSuite` bucket and the typed selection face each take a second row with no structural change.

### ④ Design judgment

Each `hits` file, judged against the code it cites and the scenario it is accepted against (a legacy ERP / MES / HIS estate on an on-premises SQL Server, federated in place, read live, written behind both opt-ins, never managed).

**`packages/spec/src/data/driver/mssql.zod.ts`** — against the factory arm (`buildMssqlConnection`, `resolveSslOption`) and the postgres contract it mirrors. Every accepted key reaches tedious under the right name; every refused key names the spelling that works; the no-URL decision is true of the client and the factory agrees. Tried to break: `encrypt: false` in `config` is renamed to `ssl` with a hint and then read as the toggle — right; `trustServerCertificate` in `config` is refused toward the datasource `ssl` block — right. The `ssl` docblock is where it breaks. **Must-fix ④.1**: the docblock says "Certificate verification lives in the datasource-level `ssl` block (`rejectUnauthorized: false` is how a server with a self-signed certificate is trusted)", and the SQL Server docs section repeats it as the instruction ("set the datasource-level `ssl: { rejectUnauthorized: false }` (tedious's `trustServerCertificate`)"), under an example that sets `config.ssl: true`. In the tree, `defineDatasource` parses, the block's `enabled` defaults to `false`, `resolveSslOption` returns `false` whenever a block is present with `enabled: false` (the block outranks the toggle), and `buildMssqlConnection(spec, false)` emits `options.encrypt = false` and never sets `trustServerCertificate`. An author following the spec's own sentence, in exactly the card's scenario (an on-premises server with a self-signed certificate), gets encryption turned OFF — silently against a server that does not force encryption, or a certificate error against one that does — instead of a trusted certificate. The shared guidance string the same file imports, `SSL_DETAIL_BELONGS_ON_DATASOURCE`, spells the shape that works (`ssl: { enabled: true, rejectUnauthorized: false, ca: … }`); the new prose dropped `enabled: true`. Fix the sentence in `mssql.zod.ts` and the docs section (and the example), or make the refusal text for `trustServerCertificate` carry the full shape. A published contract whose prescribed shape downgrades transport security is a must-fix.

**`packages/spec/src/data/driver/config-registry.zod.ts`** — against ADR-0015 §4.6 and its first consumers (`datasource.zod.ts`, the two boot hosts through `resolveDatabaseDriverId`, the factory's `kind` switch). The `federationOnly` column derives the authoring refusal and the typed selection face from one table rather than hand-listing at a consumer, which is the file's own rule and the right generalisation for the Oracle row.
